newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- quiet, off 1/8 to 1/4.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- quiet, off 1/8 to 1/4.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds were quoted 1/8 to 1/4 lower at midday, as traders said the new issue market was grabbing most of the attention.

Secondary action continued to dwindle, with the Blue List of offerings dropping to an unusually low $886 million. "There's not too much going on," one trader said. But she added that there was good follow-through action on new issues.
The day's largest new issue came from Bear Stearns & Co., which said it tentatively priced Puerto Rico Electric Power Authority's $469 million power bond issue at a top yield of 5.68 percent in 2027.
Orange County, Fla., sold $351 million certificates of participation through PaineWebber Inc., which priced the bonds with a 5.782 percent yield in 2022.
In competitive action, J.P. Morgan Securities Inc. won Tennessee's $173 million general obligation issue, and reoffered the 2017 bonds at a 5.45 percent yield.
J.P. Morgan said at midday it had a $30.3 million balance, indicating good demand.
New offerings were expected to total nearly $4.1 billion this week, and traders said demand has so far been good.

Treasury bonds were also lower, after morning data releases showed first quarter labor cost figures were higher than expected. In addition, supply concern surrounding Wednesday's auction of $12 billion of 10-year notes was weighing on prices.

In the muni secondary market, Dade County, Fla., water and sewer FGIC 5-1/4s of 2026 were bid at 5.74 percent, up two basis points from Tuesday. Upper Occoquan Sewer Authority Va., MBIA 5.0s of 2025 were down two basis points to 5.74 percent.
In debt futures, June municipal bond futures lost 10/32 to 114-31/32, while June Treasury bonds dropped 16/32 to 109-19/32. The MOB spread widened to 172 ticks from 166 at the close Tuesday.
